title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): a regular n-gon P_n on a complex projective line Σ is built from a regular 2n-gon P̃_{2n}. The 2n-gon is centred at the origin of a real plane V = V_{P̃_{2n}}. One sets Σ = P(V)(C), and P_n = P̃_{2n}/{±1}, where -1 acts on P̃_{2n} by the antipodal map. Each vertex s̃ is sent to the line R·s̃. Antipodal vertices give the same line, so S = S̃/±1 embeds as n equally spaced points on the real circle Σ_R = P(V)(R).

This page:
(6) D_{P̃_{2n}} := Aut_comb(P̃_{2n}) is the dihedral group of order 4n (Grothendieck writes D_{2n}). It acts linearly on V through the symmetries of the polygon, hence on P(V) and on Σ. The central element -1 (rotation by π) acts trivially on the projective line. So the action factors through D_{P̃_{2n}}/{±1}.
(7) This quotient is D_{P_n} = Aut_comb(P_n), dihedral of order 2n. Its induced action on Σ = Σ_{P_n} coincides with the action by transport of structure when Σ is regarded as attached directly to P_n. This is the point of the previous page's remark that Σ_{P̃_{2n}} depends only on P_n.
(8) For n odd, the canonical extension 1 → {±1} → D_{P̃_{2n}} → D_{P_n} → 1 splits, but not canonically. A splitting is given by choosing one of the two inscribed n-gons P'_n, P''_n formed by alternate vertices. Its stabiliser is an index-2 dihedral subgroup of order 2n mapping isomorphically to D_{P_n}. It does not contain -1, because for n odd the antipodal map sends vertex k to k+n, which has the other parity, and so swaps P'_n and P''_n. Hence D_{4n} ≅ D_{2n} × Z/2 for n odd.
The figure illustrates n = 3: a hexagon with the two triangles ABC and A'B'C', with A, A' antipodal.
The page ends announcing an equivalence of categories for n odd, carried out on the next page: pairs (2n-gon, marked n-subgon) ↔ n-gons. That page then deduces Σ_{P_n} ≅ P(V_{P_n}) directly, since for n odd the vertices of an n-gon give distinct lines.

Purpose: a careful, functorial ('canonical') construction of the standard dihedrally symmetric configuration of n points on P^1. It serves as a building block for the 'Teichmülleries': dihedral/cyclic symmetries of M_{0,n}, real cells, and the Teichmüller tower and lego.
errors: No mathematical errors. Note for completeness: for n even the extension (8) does not split. A lift of a generating rotation of D_n is r or -r, and both have order 2n. Grothendieck's restriction to n odd is therefore exactly right.
Minor: in the parenthesis about the figure the manuscript appears to read 'pour n = 6'. Since 2n = 6 here, the case illustrated is n = 3 (two triangles); this is a slip of the pen or a misreading.

ideas.what: The linear action of the dihedral group of the 2n-gon on the plane descends to a projective action of the quotient by the centre ±1, which is the dihedral group of the n-gon. It agrees with the action by transport of structure.
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral subgroups of PGL_2 / PO(2) acting on P^1 with a real regular polygon orbit
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (finite subgroups of PGL_2 and their configurations on P^1); not explicitly

ideas.what: For n odd, D_{4n} ≅ D_{2n} × {±1}. The splitting is non-canonical and corresponds to the choice of one of the two inscribed n-gons.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of central extension of dihedral groups for odd n

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories for n odd: (2n-gon with a marked n-subgon) ↔ n-gon.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary groupoid equivalence of combinatorial polygons

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary bookkeeping of dihedral symmetries for a canonical regular-polygon configuration on P^1. Everything is classical; it is only interesting as an illustration of Grothendieck's insistence on canonicity (non-canonical splitting tied to a choice of sub-polygon).
transcription_corrections: The parenthesis reads '(pour n = 6, le choix d'un des deux triangles' in the image (the machine gave 'n = 3[?]'). The case meant is 2n = 6, i.e. n = 3.
Title: 'La représentation naturelle des D_{P̃}' — the D is written as a blackboard/bold letter, consistent with the notation 𝔻_{2n} used for the abstract dihedral group in (6).
